sentences.text:
1 PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant alongwith six other co-accused persons is stated to have taken an amount of Rs. 12 lakhs each for getting appointed the three persons in Indian Railways, as such, the total amount of Rs. 36 lakhs was usurped by the applicant on the false promise of appointment in the said department.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.

6. The applicant was granted anticipatory bail till the submission of report u/s 173(2) Cr.P.C. vide order dated 17.8.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No.
2667 of 2023 and he has not misused the said opportunity granted.
7. The applicant, as a bonafide act, had given the cheques to the informant, which bounced, but he has not initiated any proceedings u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act.
Rather, he has instituted the instant FIR, which is nothing but the abuse of process of Court.
8. Not a single penny has been transferred to the account of the applicant.
The amount of Rs. 15 thousand each has been transferred to the account of the co-accused persons Rajesh and Atul.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY:
10.

The prayer for anticipatory bail has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history has not been disputed.
CONCLUSION:

11. Relying on its judgement passed in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273, the Supreme Court in Md. Asfak Alam Vs. State of Jharkhand and another (2023) 8 SCC 632 has stated that once the charge-sheet was filed and there was no impediment, at least on the part of the accused, the court having regard to the nature of the offences, the allegations and the maximum sentence of the offences they were likely to carry, ought to have granted the bail as a matter of course.

However, the court did not do so but mechanically rejected and, virtually, to rub salt in the Pushpendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131746303/
2 wound directed the appellant to surrender and seek regular bail before the trial court.

sentences.text: Thus, the High Court fell into error in adopting such a casual approach.

12. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

16. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
